inputs.userGoal: Deploy Azure network, different databases in that network to act as source databases, and then populate with test schemas and data. Create everything as IaC so I can easily spin it up for demo purposes.
subGoals: Balanced persistent demo lab: prioritize isolation, repeatability, and reasonable cost over production availability.
Private source databases: expose SSH only to one administrator CIDR and reserve later connectivity for a separately deployed discovery agent.
Representative coverage: deploy the six source engines with immediately available legal media and reserve Sybase for licensed media later.

reasoning.whyChosen: Provides one explicit lifecycle and teardown boundary for every persistent demo-lab resource.
alternativesConsidered: Deploy into an existing resource group
Separate resource groups for network and compute
reasoning.tradeoffs: A single resource group makes full teardown simple but does not separate operator permissions by resource class.

reasoning.whyChosen: Provides one stable least-privilege identity for both VM bootstrap processes to retrieve secrets without embedding credentials in cloud-init.
alternativesConsidered: Credentials embedded in secure ARM parameters only
reasoning.tradeoffs: A shared bootstrap identity has a wider scope than per-VM identities but keeps the small demo lab manageable; it receives only Key Vault secret read access.

resources.name: kv-dbmlab

reasoning.whyChosen: Keeps database bootstrap credentials out of repository files and deployment outputs while supporting VM managed-identity retrieval.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Public network access is enabled for simple ARM and VM retrieval in this isolated demo; Azure RBAC, purge protection, soft delete, and secret-only permissions remain enabled.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The identity is created before its Key Vault role assignments and secret retrieval path are configured.

resources.name: kvrole-dbmlab-bootstrap

reasoning.whyChosen: Grants the shared VM bootstrap identity read-only access to secret values without granting secret management permissions.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Both VMs can read both lab bootstrap secrets; per-VM identities would narrow access but add operational overhead.

resources.dependencyReasoning: Both the principal and Key Vault scope must exist before the assignment is created.

resources.name: database-admin-password

reasoning.whyChosen: Materializes a secure deployment parameter for deterministic container bootstrap without exposing it in repository files or outputs.
alternativesConsidered: Use a separate credential for every engine
reasoning.tradeoffs: One shared synthetic credential simplifies demo operation but must never be reused outside this isolated lab.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The parent vault must exist before the secret is stored.

resources.name: oracle-sys-password

reasoning.whyChosen: Keeps the Oracle SYS bootstrap credential out of cloud-init, repository files, and deployment outputs.
alternativesConsidered: Embed the value through cloud-init substitution
reasoning.tradeoffs: A second secure parameter adds one deployment prompt but separates privileged Oracle administration from demo users.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The parent vault must exist before the secret is stored.

resources.name: vnet-dbmlab

reasoning.whyChosen: Creates a non-overlapping address space with ample room for later agent, VPN, or peering subnets without changing database addresses.
alternativesConsidered: One public VM without a VNet design
reasoning.tradeoffs: A single VNet and database subnet are sufficient until agent or hybrid connectivity is introduced.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The database subnet is associated with the NSG when created.

inboundRules: Allow TCP 1433, 1521, 3306, 5432, 9042, and 27017 only from VirtualNetwork
outboundRules: Use platform defaults for package and container image retrieval

reasoning.whyChosen: Enforces the primary requirement that database listeners remain private while administrators can SSH only from one explicit CIDR.
alternativesConsidered: Public database ports restricted by source IP
reasoning.tradeoffs: Outbound traffic is not force-tunneled or inspected in this phase; that can be added when the network is integrated with an enterprise landing zone.

resources.name: pip-dbmlab-engine
resources.subtype: Allowlisted SSH endpoint for multi-engine host

reasoning.whyChosen: Provides controlled administrative SSH access and direct outbound Internet access for initial container image retrieval.
alternativesConsidered: No public IP with NAT Gateway and Run Command
reasoning.tradeoffs: A public IP increases exposure but the NSG permits only SSH from adminSourceCidr; no database listener is public.

resources.name: pip-dbmlab-oracle
resources.subtype: Allowlisted SSH endpoint for Oracle host

reasoning.whyChosen: Provides controlled administrative SSH access and package retrieval for the Oracle host.
reasoning.tradeoffs: The Oracle host has a public IP for SSH only; Oracle listener and EM Express remain private.

resources.name: nic-dbmlab-engine

reasoning.whyChosen: A stable private address gives future discovery agents and generated inventories a predictable endpoint.
reasoning.tradeoffs: The fixed address is simple for a two-host lab; private DNS can be added with later network integration.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The NIC attaches to the database subnet and its Standard public IP.

resources.name: nic-dbmlab-oracle

reasoning.whyChosen: A stable private Oracle listener address supports repeatable inventory and collector configuration.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Static addressing requires subnet coordination but is straightforward in the reserved /24.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The NIC attaches to the database subnet and its Standard public IP.

reasoning.whyChosen: Separates persistent database volumes from the OS disk and provides adequate capacity for representative synthetic data at lower cost than Premium SSD.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Standard SSD limits throughput for load testing but is sufficient for metadata discovery and demos.

reasoning.whyChosen: Keeps Oracle data separate from the OS image and leaves room for XE demo schemas and generated workload data.
reasoning.tradeoffs: The lab favors cost and reproducibility over database IOPS.

resources.name: vm-dbmlab-engine

properties.seedContract: Idempotent cloud-init writes versioned Docker Compose and engine seed files, mounts the data disk, starts health-checked containers with memory limits, creates representative migration-assessment schemas and synthetic data in SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, and Cassandra, grants assessment_reader access, and writes /opt/dbmigration-lab/READY only after every seed verification passes.

reasoning.whyChosen: This East US 2 subscription explicitly permits the memory-optimized constrained-vCPU E4-2ads v7 SKU, which better fits concurrent database containers than the available two-vCPU general-purpose choices.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Five engines share one failure and performance boundary. This is appropriate for collector tests but not comparative load benchmarks.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The VM requires identity, secret authorization, NIC, and data disk before bootstrap can run.

resources.name: vm-dbmlab-oracle

properties.securityType: TrustedLaunch when marketplace image supports it
properties.seedContract: Idempotent cloud-init installs Oracle XE from Oracle repositories, configures XEPDB1, creates representative migration-assessment schema objects and synthetic data, grants assessment_reader access, validates listener/schema/data readiness, and writes /opt/dbmigration-lab/READY.

reasoning.whyChosen: A dedicated Oracle Linux host isolates Oracle installation and licensing characteristics while the allowed E2ads v7 SKU provides a small persistent demo footprint.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Oracle XE is representative for schema discovery but does not expose every Enterprise Edition feature or production topology.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The VM requires identity, secret authorization, NIC, and data disk before bootstrap can run.

references.title: Oracle workloads on Azure virtual machines

overallReasoning.summary: A separate East US 2 demo resource group contains an isolated database VNet and two Linux hosts: a multi-engine container host and an Oracle XE host. Secure, deterministic provisioning creates representative migration-assessment schemas and synthetic data without exposing database ports publicly.
overallReasoning.tradeoffs: This reconstructable non-production lab intentionally uses one instance per host with no availability zones, backup, disaster recovery, VPN, Bastion, Azure Firewall, DDoS Network Protection, or monitoring. SSH uses two Standard public IPs restricted to one CIDR. Sybase ASE is deferred because licensed installation media is not currently available. Key Vault public network access remains enabled for ARM deployment and VM secret retrieval, with Azure RBAC and no secrets in outputs.

wafReview.identity: A user-assigned managed identity retrieves database bootstrap secrets from Key Vault.
wafReview.secrets: Secure deployment parameters are written to Key Vault; credentials are never committed or emitted as deployment outputs.
wafReview.network: Database ports are reachable only inside the VNet. Public ingress is limited to TCP 22 from the administrator CIDR.
wafReview.encryption: Azure managed disks are encrypted at rest and database clients can enable engine-supported TLS after provisioning.
wafReview.resilience: Single-instance hosts and reconstructable seed data are accepted because the lab has no production SLO.
wafReview.tagging: Every resource receives project, environment, workload, and lifecycle tags.

plan.validation: The design is coherent for subscription 7ee7fa4f-8359-4fb9-ac34-361728102038 in East US 2: quota exists for two VMs and network resources, all VM/NIC/disk pairs are co-located, Standard public IPs use static allocation, subnet CIDRs are non-overlapping, database ports are private, no monitoring resources are included, and every dependency resolves without cycles. Exact Oracle marketplace image and Trusted Launch compatibility must be revalidated during Bicep compilation or deployment preflight.
architecturePrinciples: Secrets outside source control and outputs
